Now I have the regression test cases. The first one is:
```
    codeblock
> [!note]
> foo
```

This is the input that triggers the bug. Let me understand why. The `    codeblock` is an indented code block. Then `> [!note]` is an admonition inside a blockquote.

Let me trace through this:
1. `    codeblock` - indented code block. `pivot_line = &md_dummy_blank_line`, `line = &line_buf[0]`. `md_analyze_line` fills `line_buf[0]` with `MD_LINE_INDENTEDCODE`. `md_process_line` sets `*p_pivot_line = line` (line_buf[0]).
2. `> [!note]` - this is inside a blockquote. `line == pivot_line` (both line_buf[0]), so `line` switches to `line_buf[1]`. `md_analyze_line` fills `line_buf[1]`. Since `pivot_line->type == MD_LINE_INDENTEDCODE`, the line is analyzed as indented code continuation? No wait, the `>` makes it a blockquote.

Actually, let me think about this more carefully. The `    codeblock` is an indented code block. Then `> [!note]` starts a blockquote. The `>` is a blockquote mark.

In `md_analyze_line`, the blockquote mark `>` is processed. Since `pivot_line->type == MD_LINE_INDENTEDCODE`, the line might be treated as indented code continuation. But the `>` makes it a blockquote.

Hmm, this is getting complex. Let me just try to run the harness with this input and see if it crashes.
